steps.title: Open the Factor Lab
steps.narration: We open the Factor Lab — a read-only research page that grades each stock signal against months of already-recorded forward returns, so nothing here is a guess or a prediction.
steps.point_out: The decile sort and rank-IC score at the top judge one factor at a time. The brand-new tool we are here to see sits at the very bottom of the page.

steps.title: Compare a combined cohort against the baseline and each single factor
steps.narration: At the bottom is the new Multi-factor combination cohort panel. Each condition is a factor set to the top or bottom of its range — here we switch the first one to the bottom, and the comparison recomputes on the spot.
steps.point_out: Four rows to compare: the all-names baseline, one row per single factor, and the shaded Combined (AND) cohort — each with its sample size, mean and median forward return, hit-rate, and downside risk-adjusted return.

steps.title: Stack a third condition
steps.narration: We add a third condition, and the comparison grows to three single factors plus the cohort that satisfies all of them at once.
steps.point_out: The combined cohort's sample size is never larger than the smallest single factor — stacking filters can only narrow the group. The Add condition button greys out once three conditions are in play.

steps.title: Pare back to two conditions
steps.narration: Removing a condition snaps the table back to two factors plus their combined cohort.
steps.point_out: Add condition is selectable again, and the Remove buttons grey out at two conditions — the tool never lets you drop below a real side-by-side comparison.

steps.title: One shared horizon re-points every table
steps.narration: One shared horizon control at the top of the page sets the holding period for everything at once — switch it and the decile sort, the regime table, and this new combination table all re-point together.
steps.point_out: Your chosen conditions carry over unchanged across the horizon switch; only the numbers update.

steps.title: Honest NA instead of invented numbers
steps.narration: Honesty is built in: set two conditions to opposite extremes and the combined group can genuinely run out of matching names. When that happens the cells simply read NA beside the real sample size.
steps.point_out: A thin or empty cohort shows NA with its true count — never an invented 0.00% return.

steps.title: One date control — the lab is a cross-date aggregate
steps.narration: Finally, the global as-of date in the header never touches this page. The Factor Lab pools its evidence across every date, so changing that date leaves all of its tables exactly as they were.
steps.point_out: There is just one date control in the whole product — this research page deliberately adds none of its own.
